rv.q: Although the escape routines don’t necessarily align with the sins exactly, there are loose connections (you’ll remember the stunts more than the themes).
All of those elements are portrayed with great skill separately, but together in this rendition, they lack a cohesiveness...
And while nobody expects a high-brow dramatic interpretation of the Seven Deadly Sins, Marta Lucata (concept and script) and director Alberto Oliva fail to stir up any sense of thematic urgency.
Most of the magic is mediocre, the contraptions can be confusing, and Lord Nil’s celebrations are right out of professional wrestling.

cn.t: Critics find this escape-artist spectacle visually ambitious but structurally hollow, with the seven deadly sins theme feeling disconnected from the stunts and awkward narration undermining the theatrical experience.
